comments.text: Hey Cory, not sure if you’ll see this - but I caught what you said at the beginning. I’m a Registered Dental Hygienist - the sloughing of the tissues in your mouth could be a couple things. You might be allergic/sensitive to an ingredient called SLS (Sodium Lauryl Sulfate) in your toothpaste. It’s an ingredient used to clean off plaque bacteria, and to foam up your mouth to give you that “more clean” feeling. Another option is if you use a mouth rinse, you might be sensitive to the alcohol in it if you’re not using “alcohol free”. I’d try experimenting with SLS free toothpastes or alcohol free mouthwash! Glad you’re back ❤

comments.text: Hey, Cory! So next week, I'm going up to Michigan and when I told I was, I automatically thought of you. I've been watching you since 2023 and it has been a BLESSING.
